{{for|the Hungarian Olympic diver|András Hajnal (diver)}}
{{short description|Hungarian set theorist}}
[[File:Hajnal András 2012-09-09.jpg|thumb|Image of Hajnal András (Photo: ''Mihály Hujter'')]]
'''András Hajnal''' (May 13, 1931 – July 30, 2016<ref>[https://www.facebook.com/809060619130294/photos/a.857845014251854.1073741828.809060619130294/1061525430550477/?type=1&theater Announcement from Rényi Institute]</ref><ref>[http://dimacs.rutgers.edu/DIMACS_highlights/hajnal/hajnal.html Remembering András Hajnal (1931-2016)]</ref>) was a professor of mathematics at [[Rutgers University]]<ref>[http://math.rutgers.edu/people/index.php?type=faculty-emeritus&id=149 Rutgers University Department of Mathematics – Emeritus Faculty] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100715123824/http://math.rutgers.edu/people/index.php?type=faculty-emeritus&id=149 |date=2010-07-15 }}.</ref> and a member of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]]<ref>[http://www.math.bme.hu/akademia/akada.html Hungarian Academy of Sciences, Section for Mathematics] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090311073142/http://www.math.bme.hu/akademia/akada.html |date=March 11, 2009 }}.</ref> known for his work in [[set theory]] and [[combinatorics]].

==Biography==
Hajnal was born on 13 May 1931,<ref name="cv">[http://www.renyi.hu/~ahajnal/hajn2006.pdf Curriculum vitae].</ref> in [[Budapest]], [[Kingdom of Hungary (1920–1946)|Hungary]].

He received his university diploma (M.Sc. degree) in 1953 from the [[Eötvös Loránd University]],<ref>[http://www.epa.oszk.hu/00700/00775/00029/448-456.html A halmazelmélet huszadik századi "Hajnal A"], M. Streho's interview with A. H., ''[[Magyar Tudomány]]'', 2001.</ref> his [[Candidate of Sciences|Candidate]] of Mathematical Science degree (roughly equivalent to Ph.D.) in 1957, under the supervision of [[László Kalmár]],<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=24611|name=Andras Hajnal}}. The 1957 date is from Hajnal's cv; the mathematics genealogy site lists the date of Hajnal's Ph.D. as 1956.</ref> and his Doctor of Mathematical Science degree in 1962. From 1956 to 1995 he was a faculty member at the [[Eötvös Loránd University]]; in 1994, he moved to Rutgers University to become the director of [[DIMACS]], and he remained there as a professor until his retirement in 2004.<ref name="cv"/> He became a member of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences in 1982, and directed its [[Alfréd Rényi Institute of Mathematics|mathematical institute]] from 1982 to 1992.<ref name="cv"/> He was general secretary of the [[János Bolyai Mathematical Society]] from 1980 to 1990, and president of the society from 1990 to 1994.<ref name="cv"/> Starting in 1981, he was an advisory editor of the journal ''[[Combinatorica]]''. Hajnal was also one of the honorary presidents of the European Set Theory Society.

Hajnal was an avid [[chess]] player.<ref>[http://atlas-conferences.com/f/a/b/c/58.dir/second.txt The announcement] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080724013925/http://atlas-conferences.com/f/a/b/c/58.dir/second.txt |date=2008-07-24 }} for the 2001 conference in honor of Hajnal and Sós calls him "the great chess player"; the conference included a blitz chess tournament in his honor.</ref>

Hajnal was the father of [[Peter Hajnal]], the co-dean of the [[European College of Liberal Arts]].

==Research and publications==
Hajnal was the author of over 150 publications.<ref>[http://www.math.rutgers.edu/~ahajnal/hajnalpu.pdf List of publications] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100716114722/http://www.math.rutgers.edu/~ahajnal/hajnalpu.pdf |date=July 16, 2010 }} from Hajnal's web site.</ref> Among the many co-authors of [[Paul Erdős]], he had the second largest number of joint papers, 56.<ref>[https://files.oakland.edu/users/grossman/enp/Erdos0p.html List of collaborators of Erdős by number of joint papers], from the Erdős number project web site.</ref>
With Peter Hamburger, he wrote a textbook, ''Set Theory'' (Cambridge University Press, 1999, {{ISBN|0-521-59667-X}}). Some of his more well-cited research papers<ref>According to citation counts from Google scholar, retrieved March 1, 2009.</ref> include
*A paper on [[circuit complexity]] with Maas, Pudlak, [[Mario Szegedy|Szegedy]], and György Turán,<ref>{{citation|contribution=Threshold circuits of bounded depth|first1=A.|last1=Hajnal|first2=W.|last2=Maass|first3=P.|last3=Pudlak|first4=M.|last4=Szegedy|first5=G.|last5=Turán|title=[[Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science|Proc. 28th Symp. Foundations of Computer Science (FOCS 1987)]]|pages=99–110|year=1987|doi=10.1109/SFCS.1987.59|isbn=0-8186-0807-2 |s2cid=9206369}}</ref> showing exponential lower bounds on the size of bounded-depth circuits with weighted [[majority function|majority]] gates that solve the problem of computing the [[parity (mathematics)|parity]] of [[dot product|inner products]].
*The [[Hajnal–Szemerédi theorem]] on [[equitable coloring]], proving a 1964 conjecture of Erdős:<ref>{{citation|contribution=Proof of a conjecture of P. Erdős|first1=A.|last1=Hajnal|first2=E.|last2=Szemerédi|author2-link=Endre Szemerédi|title=Combinatorial theory and its applications, II (Proc. Colloq., Balatonfüred, 1969)|publisher=North-Holland|year=1970|pages=601–623|mr=0297607}}</ref> let Δ denote the maximum degree of a vertex in a finite graph ''G''. Then ''G'' can be [[graph coloring|colored]] with Δ&nbsp;+&nbsp;1 colors in such a way that the sizes of the color classes differ by at most one. Several authors have subsequently published simplifications and generalizations of this result.<ref>{{citation | last = Catlin | first = Paul A. | journal = Utilitas Mathematica | pages = 163–177 | title = On the Hajnal–Szemerédi theorem on disjoint cliques | volume = 17 | year = 1980 | mr = 583138}}; {{citation | last = Fischer | first = Eldar | doi = 10.1002/(SICI)1097-0118(199908)31:4<275::AID-JGT2>3.0.CO;2-F | issue = 4 | journal = [[Journal of Graph Theory]] | pages = 275–282 | title = Variants of the Hajnal–Szemerédi theorem | volume = 31 | year = 1999 | mr = 1698745}}; {{citation | last1 = Kierstead | first1 = H. A. | last2 = Kostochka | first2 = A. V. | doi = 10.1017/S0963548307008619 | issue = 2 | journal = [[Combinatorics, Probability and Computing]] | pages = 265–270 | title = A short proof of the Hajnal–Szemerédi theorem on equitable colouring | volume = 17 | year = 2008 | mr = 2396352| s2cid = 12254683 }}; {{citation | last1 = Martin | first1 = Ryan | last2 = Szemerédi | first2 = Endre | doi = 10.1016/j.disc.2007.08.019 | issue = 19 | journal = [[Discrete Mathematics (journal)|Discrete Mathematics]] | pages = 4337–4360 | title = Quadripartite version of the Hajnal–Szemerédi theorem | volume = 308 | year = 2008 | mr = 2433861| doi-access =  }}</ref>
*A paper with Erdős and J. W. Moon on graphs that avoid having any ''k''-[[clique (graph theory)|clique]]s. [[Turán's theorem]] characterizes the graphs of this type with the maximum number of edges; Erdős, Hajnal and Moon find a similar characterization of the smallest [[maximal element|maximal]] ''k''-clique-free graphs, showing that they take the form of certain [[split graph]]s. This paper also proves a conjecture of Erdős and [[Tibor Gallai|Gallai]] on the number of edges in a [[critical graph]] for [[dominating set|domination]].<ref>{{citation|doi=10.2307/2311408|first1=P.|last1=Erdős|author1-link=Paul Erdős|first2=A.|last2=Hajnal|first3=J. W.|last3=Moon|title=A problem in graph theory|journal=[[American Mathematical Monthly]]|volume=71|issue=10|pages=1107–1110|publisher=Mathematical Association of America|year=1964|jstor=2311408|mr=0170339|s2cid=120072868|url=https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/ec5e/9df34a4671c07d54d73e0e6b67be47cb71af.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200219050633/https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/ec5e/9df34a4671c07d54d73e0e6b67be47cb71af.pdf|archive-date=2020-02-19}}</ref>
*A paper with Erdős on [[graph coloring]] problems for infinite graphs and [[hypergraph]]s.<ref>{{citation|first1=P.|last1=Erdős|author1-link=Paul Erdős|first2=A.|last2=Hajnal|title=On chromatic number of graphs and set-systems|journal=[[Acta Mathematica Hungarica]]|volume=17|issue=1–2|pages=61–99|year=1966|doi=10.1007/BF02020444|doi-broken-date=30 January 2026 |doi-access=free|mr=0193025|s2cid=189780485}}</ref> This paper extends [[greedy coloring]] methods from finite to infinite graphs: if the vertices of a graph can be well-ordered so that each vertex has few earlier neighbors, it has low chromatic number. When every finite subgraph has an ordering of this type in which the number of previous neighbors is at most ''k'' (that is, it is [[Degeneracy (graph theory)|''k''-degenerate]]), an infinite graph has a well-ordering with at most 2''k''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;2 earlier neighbors per vertex. The paper also proves the nonexistence of infinite graphs with high finite [[Girth (graph theory)|girth]] and sufficiently large infinite chromatic number and the existence of graphs with high odd girth and infinite chromatic number.
Other selected results include:
*In his dissertation<ref>{{citation|doi=10.1007/BF02023921|doi-access=|first=A.|last=Hajnal|title=On a consistency theorem connected with the generalized continuum problem|journal=[[Acta Mathematica Academiae Scientiarum Hungaricae]]|volume=12|year=1961|pages=321–376|mr=0150046|issue=3–4|s2cid=120522353}}</ref> he introduced the models ''L''(''A'') (see [[Constructible universe#Relative constructibility|relative constructibility]]), and proved that if κ is a [[regular cardinal]] and ''A'' is a subset of κ<sup>+</sup>, then  ZFC and 2<sup>κ</sup>&nbsp;=&nbsp;κ<sup>+</sup> hold in ''L''(''A''). This can be applied to prove relative consistency results: e.g., if 2<sup>ℵ<sub>0</sub></sup>&nbsp;=&nbsp;ℵ<sub>2</sub> is consistent then so is  2<sup>ℵ<sub>0</sub></sup>&nbsp;=&nbsp;ℵ<sub>2</sub> and 2<sup>ℵ<sub>1</sub></sup>&nbsp;=&nbsp;ℵ<sub>2</sub>.
*[[Hajnal's set mapping theorem]], the solution to a conjecture of [[Stanisław Ruziewicz]].<ref>{{citation|first=A.|last=Hajnal|title=Proof of a conjecture of S. Ruziewicz|journal=Fund. Math.|volume=50|year=1961–1962|issue=2|pages=123–128|mr=0131986|doi=10.4064/fm-50-2-123-128|doi-access=free}}</ref> This work concerns functions ƒ that map the members of an infinite set ''S'' to small subsets of ''S''; more specifically, all subsets' cardinalities should be smaller than some upper bound that is itself smaller than the cardinality of ''S''. Hajnal shows that ''S'' must have an [[equinumerous]] subset in which no pair of elements ''x'' and ''y'' have ''x'' in ƒ(''y'') or ''y'' in ƒ(''x''). This result greatly extends the case ''n''&nbsp;=&nbsp;1 of [[Kuratowski's free set theorem]], which states that when ƒ maps an uncountable set to finite subsets there exists a pair ''x'', ''y'' neither of which belongs to the image of the other.
*An example of two graphs each with uncountable chromatic number, but with countably chromatic direct product.<ref>{{Citation
  | author = Hajnal, A.
  | title = The chromatic number of the product of two ℵ<sub>1</sub> chromatic graphs can be countable
  | journal = [[Combinatorica]]
  | volume = 5
  | year = 1985
  | pages = 137–140
  | mr = 0815579
  | doi = 10.1007/BF02579376 | doi-access=
  | postscript = .
  | issue = 2| doi-broken-date = 30 January 2026
 | s2cid = 27087122
 }}</ref> That is, [[Hedetniemi's conjecture]] fails for infinite graphs.
*In a paper<ref>{{citation
| last1=Erdős | first1=P. | author-link1=Paul Erdős
| last2=Hajnal | first2=A.
| title=On a property of families of sets
| journal=[[Acta Mathematica Academiae Scientiarum Hungaricae]]
| volume=12
| date=1964
| issue=1–2 | pages=87&ndash;123
| doi=10.1007/BF02066676 | doi-broken-date=30 January 2026 | doi-access=}}</ref> with [[Paul Erdős]] he proved several results on systems of infinite sets having [[property B]].
*A paper with [[Fred Galvin]] in which<ref>{{citation|doi=10.2307/1970936|first1=F.|last1=Galvin|author1-link=Fred Galvin|first2=A.|last2=Hajnal|title=Inequalities for cardinal powers|journal=Annals of Mathematics |series=Second Series|volume=101|issue=3|year=1975|pages=491–498|jstor=1970936}}</ref> they proved that if <math>\aleph_{\omega_1}</math> is a [[limit cardinal|strong limit cardinal]] then
*:<math>2^{\aleph_{\omega_1}}<\aleph_{(2^{\aleph_1})^+}.</math>
:This was the result which initiated [[Saharon Shelah|Shelah]]'s [[PCF theory|pcf theory]].
*With [[James Earl Baumgartner]] he proved a result in infinite [[Ramsey theory]], that for every partition of the vertices of a [[complete graph]] on ω<sub>1</sub> vertices into finitely many subsets, at least one of the subsets contains a complete subgraph on α vertices, for every α&nbsp;&lt;&nbsp;ω<sub>1</sub>.<ref>{{citation | last1 = Baumgartner | first1 = J. | last2 = Hajnal | first2 = A. | issue = 3 | journal = Fundamenta Mathematicae | pages = 193–203 | title = A proof (involving Martin's axiom) of a partition relation | volume = 78 | year = 1973 | mr = 0319768 | doi=10.4064/fm-78-3-193-203| doi-access = free }}. For additional results of Baumgartner and Hajnal on partition relations, see the following two papers: {{citation | last1 = Baumgartner | first1 = J. E. | last2 = Hajnal | first2 = A. | contribution = A remark on partition relations for infinite ordinals with an application to finite combinatorics | location = Providence, RI | pages = 157–167 | publisher = Amer. Math. Soc. | series = Contemp. Math. | title = Logic and combinatorics (Arcata, Calif., 1985) | volume = 65 | year = 1987 | mr = 891246 | doi=10.1090/conm/065/891246| isbn = 978-0-8218-5052-7 }}; {{citation | last1 = Baumgartner | first1 = James E. | last2 = Hajnal | first2 = Andras | doi = 10.2307/2695046 | issue = 2 | journal = The Journal of Symbolic Logic | pages = 811–821 | title = Polarized partition relations | volume = 66 | year = 2001 | publisher = Association for Symbolic Logic | jstor = 2695046 | mr = 1833480| s2cid = 28122765 }}</ref> This can be expressed using the notation of [[partition relation]]s as
*:<math>\omega_1\to(\alpha)^2_n.</math>
*With [[Matthew Foreman]] he proved that if κ is [[measurable cardinal|measurable]] then<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Foreman | first1 = M. | last2 = Hajnal | first2 = A. | year = 2003 | title = A partition relation for successors of large cardinals | journal = Mathematische Annalen | volume = 325 | issue = 3 | pages = 583–623 | doi=10.1007/s00208-002-0323-7 | doi-broken-date = 30 January 2026 | doi-access= | s2cid = 120500400 }}</ref> the partition relation <math>\kappa^+\to(\alpha)^2</math> holds for ''α''&nbsp;<&nbsp;Ω, where Ω&nbsp;<&nbsp;''κ''<sup>+</sup> is a very large ordinal.
*With [[István Juhász (mathematician)|István Juhász]] he published several results in [[set-theoretic topology]]. They first established<ref>A. Hajnal, I. Juhász: On hereditarily &alpha;-Lindelöf and hereditarily &alpha;-separable spaces,
 ''Ann. Univ. Sci. Budapest. Eötvös Sect. Math.'', '''11'''(1968), 115&ndash;124.</ref> the existence of Hausdorff spaces which are hereditarily separable, but not hereditarily Lindelöf, or vice versa. The existence of regular spaces with these properties ([[S-space]] and [[L-space (set theoretic topology)|L-space]]) was much later settled, by [[Stevo Todorčević|Todorcevic]] and  [[Justin Tatch Moore|Moore]].

==Awards and honors==
In 1992, Hajnal was awarded the Officer's Cross of the Order of the Republic of Hungary.<ref name="cv"/> In 1999, a conference in honor of his 70th birthday was held at [[DIMACS]],<ref>{{citation|title=Set Theory: The Hajnal Conference, October 15–17, 1999 DIMACS Center|editor-first=Simon|editor-last=Thomas|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|year=1999|isbn=978-0-8218-2786-4|series=DIMACS Series in Discrete Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science|volume=58}}</ref> and a second conference honoring the 70th birthdays of both Hajnal and [[Vera Sós]] was held in 2001 in [[Budapest]].<ref>{{citation|title=More sets, graphs and numbers: a salute to Vera Sós and András Hajnal|editor1-first=Ervin|editor1-last=Győri|editor2-first=Gyula O. H.|editor2-last=Katona|editor2-link=Gyula O. H. Katona|editor3-first=László|editor3-last=Lovász|editor3-link=László Lovász|publisher=Springer-Verlag|year=2006|isbn=978-3-540-32377-8|series=Bolyai Society Mathematical Studies|volume=15}}</ref> Hajnal became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]]<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> in 2012.
